bracket: [Textbook misprint: the working above has been corrected. The book applies its Eq. (15.23), \(Q = [m_X - m_Y - m_e]c^2\), to ATOMIC masses and prints \(0.002502 \times 931.5 = 2.3306\) MeV. For a beta PLUS decay written with atomic masses two electron masses must be subtracted, not one, because the parent atom carries one more electron than the daughter and a positron is created as well. The book's value is therefore too large by exactly one electron rest energy, \(0.00055 \times 931.5 = 0.512\) MeV. The correct maximum kinetic energy is 1.818 MeV, which agrees with the accepted \(Q(\beta^{+})\) of 1.820 MeV for \(^{22}\text{Na}\).]

[Textbook misprint: the book prints Eq. (15.7) as \(E_n = -m_e Z^2 e^4 / (8\varepsilon_0 h^2 n^2)\), with \(\varepsilon_0\) to the first power. It must be \(\varepsilon_0^{2}\), as the derivation above shows and as a dimensional check confirms; with a single \(\varepsilon_0\) the expression does not even have the dimensions of energy. The same dropped square appears in the book's expression for \(h\nu\) and in Eqs. (15.9) and (15.10) on the next page, so it is one typesetting slip repeated four times.]

[Textbook misprint: the question names the "Bracket series". The series is the BRACKETT series, named after Frederick Brackett, and the book itself spells it correctly in Section 15.5 and in Fig. 15.4. The answer is unaffected.]

[Textbook answer-key error: the book prints 16.84 MeV. That value comes from combining a bare proton \((m_p = 1.00728\ \text{u})\) with ATOMIC masses for lithium and helium, which leaves one electron unaccounted for on the left-hand side: the two helium atoms carry 4 electrons while the lithium atom and a bare proton carry only 3. The printed answer is therefore too small by exactly one electron rest energy, 0.512 MeV. The correct energy released is 17.35 MeV, which is also the accepted laboratory Q value for the reaction \(^{7}\text{Li}(p,\alpha)\alpha\).]
